p: in the fifteenth year of the: John comes at the time foretold by the prophets and lays the foundation of the gospel which is exhibited unto us, setting forth the true observing of the law and free mercy in Christ, which comes after John, using also baptism which is the outward sign both of regeneration and also forgiveness of sins.
Annas and Caiaphas being the high: Josephus calls him Ananus.
appointed you: Require no more than that sum that is appointed for the tribute money.
wages: Which was paid to them partly in money and partly in food.

And as the people were in: If we would rightly and fruitfully receive the sacraments, we must neither rest in the signs, neither in him that ministers the signs, but lift up our eyes to Christ, who is the author of the sacraments, and the giver of that which is represented by the sacraments.
Whose fan is in his hand: The gospel is the fan of the world.
But Herod the tetrarch: John's preaching is confirmed with his death.
Now when all the people were: Our baptism is sanctified in the head of the Church, and Christ also by the voice of the Father is pronounced to be our everlasting King, Priest, and Prophet.

And Jesus himself began to be: Christ's lineage, according to the flesh, is traced back even to Adam, and so to God, that it might appear that it was only he whom God promised to Abraham and David, and appointed from everlasting to his Church, which is composed of all sorts of men.
